subject: Validation request — data geography, subprocessors, and deletion timelines

Subject: Initial: residency / deletion / subprocessors question

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinSecure’s procurement team asked for a concise summary we can attach to our security review. Specifically they want: 1) where customer data (requests + logs) may be processed for a US-based tenant; 2) full list of subprocessors and where they operate; 3) whether any data crosses EU/APAC boundaries and in what situations; and 4) deletion/retention timelines and proof points (SLA or audit artifacts).

Can you share a short, factual Q&A and any supporting files? We’re trying to close the security review by next Friday.

Best,
Elena
Security Programs — FinSecure

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ve pulled together a short Q&A and two supporting artifacts: a current subprocessor inventory (redwood_subprocessors_202611.pdf) and a regional processing map (processing_map_northamerica.csv). High-level answers below; aditya and our legal lead will follow up with precise SLA/deletion language and any audit evidence.

Q1 — Where is customer request data processed for a US tenant?
- Primary inference and KV cache processing occur in our US regions (us-west-2, us-east-1).
- Logs and telemetry are ingested in US regions but may be forwarded to our observability provider in the US.

Q2 — Subprocessors and locations?
- See attached PDF (redwood_subprocessors_202611.pdf) — it lists cloud infra partners (major US cloud providers), observability vendor (US), and a CDN vendor (global). Most subprocessors operate in the US; some (CDN, monitoring) have multi-region footprints.

Q3 — Cross-border transfers?
- For a contract scoped to US processing we do not route production inference to EU/APAC unless explicitly requested or if customer-configured routing requires it (e.g., geo-failover). Backups and some monitoring pipelines can traverse borders to reach vendor regions; details in the CSV.

Q4 — Retention and deletion timelines?
- Short answer: user request content is retained for 30 days by default, KV cache ephemeral by default (refreshed per session), and long-term logs retained up to 365 days depending on plan. Our legal team can provide deletion SLA language and audit links.

I’ll leave detailed confirmations and audit references to @aditya_rao (infra) and @neha_kapoor (legal). If you need a statement for procurement, we can produce a one-page attestation.

— Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_202611.pdf (PDF), processing_map_northamerica.csv (CSV)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Elena — quick technical breakdown to supplement Mina’s note. I’ve included granular notes below and attached the processing CSV for clarity.

1) Inference path (US tenant):
- Inference requests are accepted at the customer’s configured endpoint in the selected region (we set up per-tenant routing to us-west-2 by default for US tenants).
- Model execution (GPU runtime) and KV cache live in the same region to avoid extra egress.
- If a customer enables multi-region failover our router will failover to the secondary region (explicitly configured).

2) Telemetry and logging:
- High-frequency telemetry (metrics, traces) streams to our observability partner; sampling policies ensure PII is not sent. Aggregated traces and metrics may be stored in non-US regions depending on vendor retention settings (documented in the subprocessor file).

3) Backups and persistence:
- Model artifacts and snapshot backups reside in the primary region. Cross-region replication is opt-in for durability; we do not replicate customer-provided prompt payloads by default.

4) Deletion/retention specifics (for procurement language):
- Customer-generated request payloads: default retention 30 days; can be configured to 0 (no retention) on Dedicated/Private plans.
- KV cache: ephemeral — typically cleared within hours; not stored as persistent customer records.
- Audit logs: retained up to 365 days; can be shortened via contract.
- Deletion SLA: standard request processed within 5 business days; verified deletion report available.

If FinSecure needs a signed attestation (SOC2 excerpt) I’ve attached our SOC2-summary-2026.pdf and can generate the formal deletion SLA clause for the contract.

— Aditya
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: processing_map_northamerica.csv (CSV), SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (PDF)

Hi Elena — I’m Neha on Redwood Legal. Short answers in procurement-ready language below; I’ve attached a data retention matrix and included a suggested contract clause you can paste into your DPA.

1) Storage outside the US:
- We do not intentionally store unredacted customer request payloads outside the US for tenants contracted for US-only processing. Exceptions are limited to: (a) customer-enabled multi-region failover; (b) customer-requested routing to a non-US region; (c) any underlying subprocessor operational requirement where data must transit for processing — these are listed per-subprocessor in redwood_subprocessors_202611.pdf.

2) Deletion SLA (contract text):
- "Upon receipt of a verifiable deletion request from the Controller, Redwood Inference will delete customer request payloads within five (5) business days and provide a deletion confirmation report within ten (10) business days. Backups containing customer content will be purged in accordance with the backup retention policy, not to exceed thirty (30) days from the deletion request unless otherwise agreed in writing."

3) Evidence / audit artifacts:
- We can provide the SOC2 summary (attached) and a one-page attestation of current subprocessor mappings. For higher assurance we offer executed auditor reports under NDA.

If you’d like, I can convert the above deletion SLA text into a DocuSign-ready amendment and share it via the HubSpot deal link.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
